subject: Load‑needle test plan and evidence request
messages:
From: Jack Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, ops-eng@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request — evidence & methodology for endpoint stress testing

Dylan,

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement and our ops team need a compact package from Redwood that describes the exact methodology, scripts, and measured results for the endpoint stress tests you ran against v2026-04 of the model in our trial. Specific asks: 

- A short writeup of the test methodology (tooling, concurrency model, request mix, seq lengths).
- Raw (or summarized) latency/throughput metrics: p50/p95/p99, QPS ranges, and CPU/GPU utilization snapshots.
- An explanation of how you simulated cold vs warm KV cache conditions and how that affected tail latency.
- Any caveats (sampling, synthetic vs production traffic differences).
- Repro instructions we can run in our environment (we are on GCP us-west2).

We need the package by next Tuesday (2026-06-30) to move the contract forward. If you have a shorter checklist for a legal/procurement pack we can take that first, but ops will want the deeper artifacts.

Thanks,
Jack
Jack Smith
Senior SRE, Acme Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jack Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 13:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — evidence & methodology for endpoint stress testing

Jack — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a compact procurement packet plus the full reproducible artifact set. Tentative plan: 

1) Procurement packet (pdf) — executive summary, p50/p95/p99 tables across three concurrency points (50, 200, 800 qps) and short notes on sampling.
2) Evidence artifacts (tarball) — JMeter/Gatling scripts, collected CSVs, GPU utilization logs, and the script we used to toggle KV cache warm/cold.
3) Repro guide — step‑by‑step for running a single-node reproduce on GCP us-west2 plus a scaled-cluster procedure.

Quick clarifying questions to ensure the artifact matches your needs: 
- For concurrency points, do you prefer absolute QPS targets or per-replica concurrency? We used QPS in our tests but can provide both.
- Do you want raw traces (full per-request latencies) or aggregated bucketed histograms (we typically share histograms to avoid PII/noise)?
- Any constraint on sharing kernel-level metrics (nvidia-smi snapshots)? We can redact instance ids but keep utilization numbers.

I’ll coordinate with Marcus to assemble the artifacts and with Monica on the delivery timeline. Expect first draft artifacts tomorrow EOD.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jack Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 10:05:30 -0700
Subject: Load‑needle test artifacts (preliminary)

Jack / team — attaching the preliminary artifacts to address Dylan's plan. Attached: redwood_load_needle_results_q2.pdf (summary), stress-script-v1.tar.gz (load scripts), repro-instructions.md (step-by-step). Also dropped an export to Drive for larger CSVs — link below.

Highlights from the summary: 
- Test sweep: targeted qps points at 25, 100, 400, 1200 across three instance classes (g4dn‑xlarge equiv).
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 under the 400 QPS steady state: 18ms / 72ms / 210ms (cold-cache p99 observed ~1.1s). 
- Throughput sustainability: we sustained 1200 qps for 15m windows with backpressure-triggered graceful degradation — CPU and GPU utilization peaked at 78%/72%.
- KV cache behavior: warm cache reduced p99 by ~62% on chat-style prompts with longer context. We include the cache‑warming script in the tarball.

Notes on methodology: we used a mixture of synthetic short prompts and realistic long-context prompts (50–512 tokens) to reflect production distribution you shared in the discovery deck. Scripts include options for constant QPS and Poisson burst profiles to emulate surge behavior.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD_redwood-load-evidence

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_load_needle_results_q2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
- stress-script-v1.tar.gz (gzip, 8MB)
- repro-instructions.md (text, 4KB)

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough to step through the scripts and the histograms.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Load‑needle test artifacts (preliminary) — formal evidence package and reproduction notes

Jack / Procurement team — forwarding the package formally. We included a short reproduction checklist so your ops team can run the load‑needle test in a contained environment. Key items included in repro-instructions.md:

- GCP instance types and AMI baseline (ubuntu + nvidia drivers we used).
- Docker compose files for the inference service and the driver.
- Commands to warm KV cache and to flip to cold-run.
- Expected artifacts and where to find p50/p95/p99 histograms.

If you want us to run the reproduce on your GCP project under an NDA, we can do a jointly run session and capture the telemetry for your records. Otherwise, the attached artifacts and Drive export should be sufficient for procurement and ops to validate.

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement confirms receipt and whether any redaction is required.
2) Ops confirms which reproduction path they prefer (self-run vs joint session).
3) We schedule optional 30m walkthrough the week of 2026-07-06.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
